![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063256/assets/4628a6e45445a585361f7d32586b27e29bc726d4ed8b7f072679e5537df59644.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,x+1\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,3x}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=x+1$ and *below* the line $y=3x.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>x+1,\,y<3x.
$$

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
x+1<y<3x.
$$

We must also include the line $y=3x$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
x+1<y\le 3x
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,x+1<y\le 3x}.
$$
